name: Hongshan
place: the Liao river and the hills of Inner Mongolia
desc: Millet farmers and hunters of north-east China, master carvers of jade, who made curled 'pig-dragons', built round and square stone altars, and kept a temple where a clay goddess looked out with eyes of jade.
source: Excavations at Niuheliang (from 1983) and Hongshanhou near Chifeng

cautious: ground a jade ring with sand and water for a whole winter
devout: painted the goddess's lips red before the spring rite
belligerent: tracked a wild boar for three days through the oak woods

inventions.name: Jade Carving
inventions.source: Hongshan jades, ground and drilled with sand abrasives: pig-dragons, hooked clouds, turtles and birds
inventions.desc: Jade too hard to cut, ground for months with sand and water into curled dragons and clouds: rites bring 15% more devotion, +1 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs nephrite jade and Polished Stone Tools.

inventions.name: Stone Cairn Tombs
inventions.source: The cairns of Niuheliang: stone-lined graves under mounds edged with painted pottery cylinders
inventions.desc: Mounds of stone over the graves of the great, ringed with painted clay tubes: rites bring 10% more devotion, and people see a little farther.
inventions.hint: Comes from building and the rites.

inventions.name: Round and Square Altars
inventions.source: Stone altars at Niuheliang in three stepped circles, beside square ones, perhaps for heaven and earth
inventions.desc: A round altar for the sky and a square one for the earth, laid out in stone: a little more lore, rites bring 5% more devotion.

inventions.name: Painted Pottery
inventions.desc: Red pots painted with black hooks and scales: the stores hold 15 more, +1 mood.

foods.name: Millet with Pine Nuts
foods.desc: Millet cooked with rich pine nuts from the forest: hunger grows 10% slower.

foods.name: Smoked Boar
foods.desc: Wild boar smoked over oak for the winter: food spoils 10% slower, +1 mood.

finds.name: Nephrite Jade
finds.source: Hongshan jade came from the Xiuyan deposits of Liaoning and other sources
finds.desc: Green stone so tough it cannot be chipped, only ground: each load is lore.

finds.name: Korean Pine
finds.desc: Great pines whose cones are full of rich, oily nuts that keep all winter.

people.name: Yu Na
people.desc: Her patience is harder than the jade she grinds.
memory: carved a pig-dragon so smooth it felt like water

people.name: Hada Gu
people.desc: He wears the tusks of every boar he has killed.
memory: killed a boar with a single spear-thrust in the snow

people.name: The Goddess of Niuheliang
people.source: A life-size clay head with inlaid jade eyes, from the 'Goddess Temple' at Niuheliang, c. 3500 BCE
people.desc: A painted clay face with green jade for eyes, found among the broken bodies of other figures in a hilltop temple.

people.name: The Jade-Bearer of the Central Cairn
people.source: Central graves at Niuheliang held a single body with jades on the chest, head and hands
people.desc: A man buried alone in the heart of a great cairn, with only jade beside him: no pots, no weapons.

people.name: Hua Yang
people.source: Hongshan painted pottery shows influence from the Yangshao culture to the south
people.text: a traveller from the great river valleys of the south, carrying painted bowls and seed millet.
memory: walked a whole season north with painted pots on my back
people.desc: A trader of the kind who carried painted pottery between Yangshao and Hongshan.

people.name: Luan
people.label: Luan, Who Speaks with the Dragon
people.desc: A shaman who wears two jade dragons on her chest. Lore 8.

people.name: Shi Ba
people.label: Shi Ba, Lord of the Cairns
people.desc: He raises hills of stone over the dead. Crafting 8.

people.name: Xiong
people.label: Xiong, the Bear-Spear
people.desc: He wears a bear's jaw as a crown. Combat 8.

events.title: A House for the Goddess
events.source: The Goddess Temple at Niuheliang, a long building on a hilltop with clay figures and a bear's jaw
events.text: The shamans want a long hall on the highest hill, with clay figures of the goddess and her companions, their eyes set with jade.

options.label: Build the temple

do.feat: Built the temple of the goddess

options.result: The goddess looks down from the hill with green eyes over all the valleys.

options.label: The open sky is enough
options.result: The rites stay under the open sky.

events.title: The Grassland Advances
events.source: A drier climate after about 3000 BCE pushed the Hongshan region toward herding
events.text: Each year the millet fields grow thinner and the grassland creeps closer. Some families want to give up farming and follow herds.

options.label: Take up herding
options.result: Some fields become pasture. The herds grow.

options.label: Hold to the fields
options.result: The fields are kept, thin as they are.

events.title: Only Jade
events.source: Hongshan's great tombs contain jades and almost nothing else, a sign that jade was the highest of gifts
events.text: A great elder has died. The jade carvers say: no pots, no weapons, only jade, laid on the chest and over the eyes, so the soul can find its way.

options.label: Bury the elder with jade
options.result: The jades go into the grave, cold and green.

options.label: Keep the jade for the living
options.result: The jades stay with the family.

tales.name: The Pig Who Became a Dragon
tales.source: A story made up around the jade 'pig-dragons'
tales.text: A little pig curled up in the snow to sleep and dreamed it was flying through the clouds. When it woke, the clouds had come down to hold it, and it was a dragon. That is why our dragons are curled like sleeping piglets, and why we carve them in green jade, the colour of the clouds before rain.
tales.moral: dreams can change what you are

tales.name: The Goddess with Jade Eyes
tales.source: A story made up around the goddess of Niuheliang
tales.text: The goddess was made of the red clay of the hill, but she had no eyes, and could not see her children. A carver gave her two pieces of the finest green jade, and then she saw everything: every hunter in the forest, every child in the cradle. She watches still.
tales.moral: the gods need us to give them eyes

tales.name: The Sky Is Round, the Earth Is Square
tales.source: A very old Chinese idea, perhaps already shown in the altars of Niuheliang
tales.text: The sky is round like a bowl turned over, and the earth beneath it is square like a field. That is why the altar for the sky is a circle and the altar for the earth is a square. Stand between them, and you stand at the middle of the world.

tales.name: The Feast of the First Snow
tales.source: A story made up around the hunting year of the north
tales.text: When the first snow falls, the hunters come back from the oak woods with boar and deer, and the whole village gathers at the cairns to eat and to tell the ancestors what the year has brought.
tales.moral: share the hunt with the ancestors
